newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk outlook may turn positive-Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk outlook may turn positive-Moody's.

text.p: NEW YORK, July 16 - The rating outlook for Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (NMK) could turn positive if the New York Public Service Commission (PSC) approves the master restructuring agreement signed on July 9th to terminate or restructure 29 Independent Power Producers (IPP) contracts.

The PSC's approval is critical as the restructuring calls for the issuance of $3.2 billion of new subordinated debt and the creation of a $4 billion regulatory asset which the company expects to recover through a transition charge. Niagara Mohawk will terminate or restructure 29 IPP contracts representing more than 80% of the company's above-market IPP costs.

NMK and certain IPPs will also enter into restructured financial and physical contracts on terms more favorable to the company than the existing contracts. Certain of the 29 IPP contracts, representing approximately 35% of IPP purchases, will be restructured on terms remaining at above-market prices.
However, these contracts are also structured to include option features and indexed cost components that Niagara Mohawk expects would provide hedges against future increase in electric market prices.

NMK would use the expected $600 million annual energy savings to repay the $3.2 billion subordinated debt over a 7 to 10-year period. The new debt would nearly double NMK's debt levels on its balance sheet and require regulators to provide revenue levels sufficient to successfully implement the master restructuring agreement.
Moody's expects the PSC, which was instrumental in promoting independent power in New York State, to favorably review NMK's restructuring proposal.
